title: Zechariah Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 7.

questions.question: In the fourth year of which king did the word of the LORD come to Zechariah?
questions.correctAnswer: King Darius
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:1 states that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah in the fourth year of king Darius.

questions.question: On which day and month did the word of the LORD come to Zechariah?
options: Fourth day of the ninth month
First day of the first month
Tenth day of the tenth month
Seventh day of the fifth month
questions.correctAnswer: Fourth day of the ninth month
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:1 specifies that the word came on the fourth day of the ninth month, even in Chisleu.

questions.question: Who were sent unto the house of God to pray before the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Sherezer and Regemmelech
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:2 mentions that Sherezer and Regemmelech, and their men, were sent to pray before the LORD.

questions.question: What was the purpose of sending Sherezer and Regemmelech to the priests and prophets?
options: To ask if they should weep in the fifth month as before
To offer sacrifices on behalf of the people
To rebuild the altar of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To ask if they should weep in the fifth month as before
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:3 shows they were sent to ask the priests and prophets whether they should weep in the fifth month as they had done for many years.

questions.question: True or False: The people asked whether they should continue separating themselves and weeping in the fifth month as in previous years.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:3 records the inquiry about continuing to weep and separate themselves in the fifth month as done in past years.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Zechariah to speak to all the people and priests regarding fasting?
options: Did they fast unto the LORD during the fifth and seventh months in the seventy years?
Should they build a new temple in Jerusalem?
Are they to offer sacrifices every month?
Must they only pray silently in their homes?
questions.correctAnswer: Did they fast unto the LORD during the fifth and seventh months in the seventy years?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:5 commands Zechariah to ask if their fasting and mourning in the fifth and seventh months for seventy years was really unto the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: According to Zechariah 7:6, when the people ate and drank, they did so for themselves and not unto the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:6 states that when the people ate and drank, they did so for themselves, not for the LORD.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:7, which prophets had the LORD cried by before?
options: The former prophets when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous
The prophets during the Babylonian exile
The prophets from the northern kingdom
The prophets after the temple was rebuilt
questions.correctAnswer: The former prophets when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:7 refers to the LORD’s words through former prophets when Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity.

questions.question: What did the LORD of hosts instruct to be executed according to Zechariah 7:9?
options: True judgment and mercy and compassion to every man
questions.correctAnswer: True judgment and mercy and compassion to every man
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:9 commands the execution of true judgment and showing mercy and compassion to one another.

questions.question: Which group is NOT mentioned in Zechariah 7:10 as people who should not be oppressed?
options: The widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The priests and Levites
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:10 lists the widow, fatherless, stranger, and poor as those not to be oppressed; priests and Levites are not mentioned here.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 7:11 says the people eagerly listened to the word of the LORD and obeyed it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:11 says the people refused to listen, pulled away their shoulder, and stopped their ears to not hear the word of the LORD.

questions.question: What did the people do to their hearts according to Zechariah 7:12?
options: Made their hearts as an adamant stone to not hear the law
Turned their hearts fully to the LORD
Loved the words of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Made their hearts as an adamant stone to not hear the law
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:12 describes the people making their hearts like adamant stone to avoid hearing the law and words of the LORD.

questions.question: What was the LORD's response when the people cried but would not hear Him, as per Zechariah 7:13?
options: He sent angels to guide them
He gave them a new law
questions.correctAnswer: He would not hear them
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:13 states that as the LORD cried and they would not hear, so when they cried, He would not hear them.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:14, what happened to the people because they refused to hear the LORD?
options: They were scattered with a whirlwind among unknown nations
They were blessed with peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They were scattered with a whirlwind among unknown nations
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:14 reveals that the LORD scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations they did not know.

questions.question: In Zechariah 7, which instruction comes first: to execute true judgment, to fast in the fifth month, to scatter the people, or to send Sherezer and Regemmelech?
options: To fast in the fifth month
questions.correctAnswer: To send Sherezer and Regemmelech
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:2 records that Sherezer and Regemmelech were sent first before the LORD’s instructions about judgment or scattering the people.

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:6, what motive does the LORD suggest people had when they ate and drank during their fasts?
options: They ate and drank to honor God
They ate and drank for themselves
They ate and drank to show humility
They ate and drank to seek forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: They ate and drank for themselves
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:6 directly states that when they ate and drank, they did so for themselves, not unto the LORD, emphasizing self-centered motives rather than true devotion. This connects with Zechariah 7:5 which questions if fasting was truly directed to the LORD.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 7:7 remind the people to listen to?
options: The words of the former prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The words of the former prophets
questions.explanation: Verse 7 emphasizes the importance of hearing the words which the LORD cried by the former prophets during times when Jerusalem was prosperous, linking the past prophetic warnings to the present situation.

questions.question: In Zechariah 7:9, what does the LORD of hosts command His people to do?
options: Execute true judgment and show mercy and compassion
questions.correctAnswer: Execute true judgment and show mercy and compassion
questions.explanation: Verse 9 instructs the people to practice justice and kindness toward one another, highlighting mercy and compassion as essential behaviors aligned with God's will.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:10, which groups should not be oppressed by the people?
options: The widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the poor
questions.correctAnswer: The widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the poor
questions.explanation: Verse 10 specifically lists these vulnerable groups who must not be oppressed, emphasizing ethical treatment of all in the community.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:11 describe the people's reaction to God's words through the prophets?
options: They refused to listen and stopped their ears
They accepted the words with joy
questions.correctAnswer: They refused to listen and stopped their ears
questions.explanation: Verse 11 reveals the people's stubbornness—they refused to heed God's message, symbolized by pulling away their shoulders and stopping their ears, showing rebellion against God's guidance.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 7:12 say about the condition of the people's hearts?
options: Their hearts were open and repentant
Their hearts were as an adamant stone
Their hearts were filled with joy
Their hearts were soft as clay
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts were as an adamant stone
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes how the people hardened their hearts like adamant stone to avoid hearing God's law, which led to the LORD's great wrath, showing spiritual obstinacy.

questions.question: What consequence does Zechariah 7:13 describe for those who refused to hear God's cry?
options: They cried but God would not hear
questions.correctAnswer: They cried but God would not hear
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains the reciprocal nature of their disobedience: as they refused to hear God's call, when they cried out themselves, God would not listen, illustrating divine justice.

questions.question: Based on Zechariah 7:5 and 7:6, what is the true purpose of fasting that the LORD expects?
options: Fasting as a public display of grief
Fasting unto the LORD with sincere devotion
questions.correctAnswer: Fasting unto the LORD with sincere devotion
questions.explanation: Verse 5 questions whether the fasting was truly directed to the LORD, while verse 6 shows that people fasted and ate for themselves. Together, they teach that fasting should be sincere worship toward God, not self-centered.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:9-10 teach about practical Christian living?
options: By commanding true judgment, mercy, and forbidding oppression
By emphasizing fasting and mourning only
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding true judgment, mercy, and forbidding oppression
questions.explanation: These verses focus on ethical behavior—justice, mercy, compassion, and protection of vulnerable people—which are key practical expressions of faith in daily life.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 7:1 specifies that the LORD's word came to Zechariah in the fourth year of King Darius.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 1 clearly states that in the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, establishing the historical context of the prophecy.

questions.question: True or False: According to Zechariah 7:14, the land was made fruitful and populous after God scattered the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states that the land was made desolate after God scattered the people with a whirlwind among nations, indicating devastation rather than fruitfulness.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 7:10 say one should not imagine against his brother in his heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: Verse 10 commands that no one should imagine evil against his brother in his heart, emphasizing purity of thought and intention in relationships.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:9-10 connect with the message of the former prophets mentioned in verse 7?
options: They both focus on temple rituals
They both emphasize fasting and prayer
They both call for justice, mercy, and protection of the vulnerable
They both warn against building walls
questions.correctAnswer: They both call for justice, mercy, and protection of the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Verse 7 references the former prophets' messages, and verses 9-10 echo those by commanding true judgment, mercy, and care for widows, orphans, strangers, and the poor, showing continuity in God's expectations.

questions.question: A believer struggles with showing mercy to others. Based on Zechariah 7:9-10, what biblical truth applies?
options: Mercy is optional in God's eyes
True judgment includes showing mercy and compassion to others
Only priests are responsible for mercy
Mercy should be shown only to friends
questions.correctAnswer: True judgment includes showing mercy and compassion to others
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 teach that executing true judgment inherently involves showing mercy and compassion to everyone, including vulnerable groups, thus mercy is a responsibility for all believers.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 7:8 introduces the LORD's word coming to Zechariah again, emphasizing the continuation of His message.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states that the word of the LORD came again to Zechariah, signaling the importance and continuity of God's communication through the prophet.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 7.

questions.question: What action did the people refuse to do according to Zechariah 7:11?
options: Hear the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Hear the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:11 states that the people 'refused to hearken, and pulled away the shoulder, and stopped their ears, that they should not hear.'

questions.question: In Zechariah 7:12, what metaphor is used to describe the hardness of the people's hearts?
questions.correctAnswer: Heart as an adamant stone
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes their hearts as 'an adamant stone,' symbolizing stubbornness and refusal to listen to God's law.

questions.question: What was the consequence of the people's refusal to listen, as described in Zechariah 7:13?
options: God also refused to hear their cries
questions.correctAnswer: God also refused to hear their cries
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:13 explains that because they would not hear when God cried, God in turn would not hear their cries.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:14, how did the LORD punish the people for their disobedience?
options: Scattered them with a whirlwind among unknown nations
Placed a curse on their crops
questions.correctAnswer: Scattered them with a whirlwind among unknown nations
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states that the LORD scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations they did not know, making the land desolate.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage contains a similar call to 'execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions' as found in Zechariah 7:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Micah 6:8
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 echoes the theme of justice, mercy, and humility before God, paralleling Zechariah 7:9's call for true judgment and compassion.

questions.question: What specific groups does Zechariah 7:10 instruct not to oppress?
questions.correctAnswer: Widow, fatherless, stranger, and poor
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:10 explicitly commands not to oppress the widow, fatherless, stranger, nor the poor.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Zechariah 7:13 where God says, 'as he cried, and they would not hear; so they cried, and I would not hear'?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:13 uses chiasmus, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order, emphasizing the reciprocal rejection between God and the people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of hardened hearts refusing God's word as in Zechariah 7:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 3:8
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:8 warns against hardening hearts as in the rebellion in the wilderness, echoing the hardened hearts in Zechariah 7:12.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:5, what question did the LORD ask about the fasting and mourning in the fifth and seventh months?
options: Did you fast unto me, even to me?
questions.correctAnswer: Did you fast unto me, even to me?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 questions whether the fasting and mourning were truly directed towards God or just for themselves.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'adamant' in Zechariah 7:12 imply about the people's hearts?
questions.correctAnswer: Extremely hard and unyielding
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'adamant' (ḥashmal) implies a very hard, unyielding substance, symbolizing stubborn refusal to listen.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:6 describe the people's attitude during times of fasting and mourning?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says they ate and drank for themselves, indicating self-centered motives rather than fasting unto God.

questions.question: Zechariah 7:7 mentions the times when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous. Does this imply the people's disobedience led to the city's desolation?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 7 contrasts the previous prosperity with later disobedience leading to desolation, implying their conduct caused judgment.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of sending Sherezer and Regemmelech to the house of God, according to Zechariah 7:2?
questions.correctAnswer: To pray before the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states they were sent to pray before the LORD in the house of God.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 7:10 warn against imagining in one's heart toward a brother?
questions.correctAnswer: Evil
questions.explanation: Verse 10 instructs that no one should imagine evil against his brother in their heart.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophet's writings are referenced as having sent words in God's spirit according to Zechariah 7:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Former prophets
questions.explanation: Verse 12 refers broadly to the 'former prophets' who spoke by God's spirit.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: In Zechariah 7:5, what critical question does God ask regarding the fasting and mourning observed for seventy years?
options: Did you fast and mourn to please Me?
Did you fast to gain wealth?
Did you fast because of the king's command?
Did you fast to follow your ancestors' customs?
questions.correctAnswer: Did you fast and mourn to please Me?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:5 asks if the fasting and mourning in the fifth and seventh months for seventy years were done unto God, emphasizing the true intent behind religious acts.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 7:6, what does the Lord imply about the people's behavior when they ate and drank during their fasts?
options: They ate and drank for themselves, not for God.
They shared their food generously with the poor.
They fasted strictly without eating or drinking.
They ate and drank as a communal sacrifice to God.
questions.correctAnswer: They ate and drank for themselves, not for God.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:6 reveals that despite fasting, the people ate and drank for their own benefit, showing a disconnect between external religious observance and internal devotion.

questions.question: What divine command regarding social ethics does Zechariah 7:9 convey?
options: Execute true judgment and show mercy and compassion to each other.
Build a temple to honor the LORD.
Separate yourselves from strangers and foreigners.
questions.correctAnswer: Execute true judgment and show mercy and compassion to each other.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:9 instructs believers to practice justice and mercy, highlighting God's demand for ethical behavior among His people.

questions.question: Which groups does Zechariah 7:10 specifically instruct the people not to oppress?
options: Foreign kings, their armies, and their people.
questions.correctAnswer: Widows, fatherless, strangers, and poor.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:10 commands protection for vulnerable groups: widows, orphans, strangers, and the poor, reflecting God's concern for social justice.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:11 describe the people's response to God's word through the former prophets?
options: They refused to listen and stopped their ears.
They eagerly accepted and obeyed the word.
They organized public ceremonies to honor it.
They debated and discussed it respectfully.
questions.correctAnswer: They refused to listen and stopped their ears.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:11 depicts the people's stubborn refusal to heed God's messages, symbolized by turning away and deafening themselves to the prophetic warnings.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Zechariah 7:12 when He speaks of making hearts 'adamant stone' and sending wrath?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and justice.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:12 shows God's holiness and justice, as He allows hardness of heart and wrath due to persistent disobedience, affirming that sin has consequences.

questions.question: What theological truth emerges from combining Zechariah 7:13 and 7:14 about God's judgment on unrepentant Israel?
options: God's judgment is just, resulting in exile and desolation when His people refuse to repent.
God punishes only those leaders who sin, sparing the people.
God uses natural disasters alone as a sign of displeasure.
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is just, resulting in exile and desolation when His people refuse to repent.
questions.explanation: Verses 7:13-14 reveal that because Israel rejected God's calls, He disciplined them through exile and desolation, underscoring the justice of God's judgment.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 7:3 reveal about the people's concern regarding their fasting tradition?
options: They questioned whether to continue weeping and fasting as before.
They wanted to introduce a new festival.
They sought to add more days to their fasting.
They planned to abandon all fasting practices.
questions.correctAnswer: They questioned whether to continue weeping and fasting as before.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:3 describes the inquiry sent to priests and prophets about maintaining the fasting and mourning on the fifth month, indicating uncertainty about its present necessity.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:7 connect the people's disobedience to historical warnings?
options: It reminds that the LORD cried through former prophets during times of prosperity.
It praises the people for heeding ancient warnings.
It introduces a new law to replace the old ones.
It states that the warnings were only for the northern kingdom.
questions.correctAnswer: It reminds that the LORD cried through former prophets during times of prosperity.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:7 emphasizes that God's prophets warned Israel in prosperous times, but the people failed to listen, showing a pattern of disobedience.

questions.question: From Zechariah 7:1, what historical context is given for the vision or word to Zechariah?
options: The fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chisleu.
The first year of King Cyrus, during the Passover.
The tenth year of King Solomon, at the Feast of Tabernacles.
The exile in Babylon, during the month of Nisan.
questions.correctAnswer: The fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chisleu.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:1 situates the prophecy precisely in time, linking it to the reign of Darius and the specific date, which is important for understanding the post-exilic context.

questions.question: What synthesis about human sin and divine patience is taught by combining Zechariah 7:11 and 7:13?
options: Human stubbornness provokes God's judgment after His patient calls are rejected.
God immediately punishes all sin without warning.
Human sin is overlooked entirely by God.
Divine patience means God never disciplines His people.
questions.correctAnswer: Human stubbornness provokes God's judgment after His patient calls are rejected.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:11 shows human refusal to listen, and 7:13 explains that because God’s calls were ignored, His judgment followed, illustrating divine patience and justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated in Zechariah 7:14 where God scatters His people with a whirlwind among unknown nations?
options: God's sovereignty over nations and history.
God's omniscience in foreseeing the future.
God's grace in forgiving sins immediately.
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over nations and history.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:14 shows God's sovereign control over the exile and scattering of Israel, using foreign nations as instruments of His judgment, demonstrating His supreme authority.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that fasting and mourning rituals in Zechariah 7 were merely superficial traditions without spiritual value. What does Zechariah 7:5-6 actually teach about the nature of true fasting?
options: True fasting must be done unto God, not for self-benefit or mere ritual.
Fasting is only about external observance without inner meaning.
Fasting is unnecessary for God's people.
Fasting is only valuable if done with elaborate ceremonies.
questions.correctAnswer: True fasting must be done unto God, not for self-benefit or mere ritual.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:5-6 emphasize that fasting loses its spiritual value if done merely for oneself rather than directed toward God, addressing the sceptic’s claim by highlighting the heart’s intent.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about God's revelation and human responsibility is evident from Zechariah 7:4 and 7:8 where the word of the LORD comes to Zechariah twice?
options: God continuously reveals His will through prophets, calling for human response.
God revealed everything only once and never again.
Prophets were free to interpret God's word as they wished.
God's word was only revealed to kings, not common people.
questions.correctAnswer: God continuously reveals His will through prophets, calling for human response.
questions.explanation: The repeated divine communication in Zechariah 7:4 and 7:8 shows God's ongoing revelation through prophets, underscoring human obligation to listen and respond.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 7:2 illustrate the communal and intercessory nature of worship post-exile?
options: Leaders and their men were sent to the house of God to pray before the LORD on behalf of the people.
Individuals fasted alone in isolation without communal involvement.
The people rejected worship and prayer entirely.
Only priests could approach God, excluding all others.
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders and their men were sent to the house of God to pray before the LORD on behalf of the people.
questions.explanation: Zechariah 7:2 shows communal leadership actively seeking God in prayer at the temple, reflecting a corporate approach to worship and intercession after the exile.
